assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Viscosity
items.clue: How thick a liquid is and how easily it flows.

items.label: Combustion
items.clue: Burning a fuel in oxygen, which releases energy.

items.label: Homologous series
items.clue: A family of similar compounds that share a general formula, such as the alkanes.

items.label: Displayed formula
items.clue: A drawing that shows every atom in a molecule and the covalent bonds between them.

questions.stem: During the combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel, what happens to the carbon and the hydrogen?

options.text: Only the carbon is oxidised, not the hydrogen
Both are reduced, because both lose oxygen
Only carbon dioxide forms, and no water
Both are oxidised, because both gain oxygen

questions.explanation: The carbon is oxidised to carbon dioxide and the hydrogen is oxidised to water, so both gain oxygen.

questions.stem: What happens to hydrocarbon molecules during cracking?

options.text: They are broken down into smaller, more useful molecules
They are separated from one another without being changed
They are joined together to make much larger molecules
They are burned to release energy and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: The specification defines cracking as breaking hydrocarbons down to produce smaller, more useful molecules.

questions.stem: Which equation shows the complete combustion of propane, C₃H₈?

options.text: 2C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 6CO₂ + 8H₂O
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
2C₃H₈ + 10O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
2C₃H₈ + 10O₂ → 6CO₂ + 10H₂O

questions.explanation: Carbon: 3 and 3. Hydrogen: 8 and 8. Oxygen: 10 and 10. The equation is balanced.

questions.stem: Which two methods of cracking does the specification name?

options.text: Catalytic cracking and fractional cracking
Steam cracking and electrolytic cracking
Catalytic cracking and steam cracking
Thermal cracking and pressure cracking

questions.explanation: These are the two methods the specification names.

questions.stem: How do the properties of hydrocarbons change as the molecules get larger?

options.text: Boiling point down, viscosity up, flammability down
Boiling point rises, viscosity down, flammability up
Boiling point falls, viscosity falls, flammability up
Boiling point up, viscosity up, flammability down

questions.explanation: Larger molecules attract each other more strongly, so they boil higher and flow less easily, and they are harder to ignite.

questions.stem: What conditions are used for catalytic cracking?

options.text: Hydrocarbons are vaporised and passed over a hot catalyst
Hydrocarbons are vaporised and mixed with steam only
Hydrocarbons are cooled and poured over a cold catalyst
Hydrocarbons are dissolved in water with a catalyst

questions.explanation: In catalytic cracking the hydrocarbon is turned into a vapour and passed over a hot catalyst.

questions.stem: How does the flammability of a hydrocarbon change as its molecules get larger?

options.text: It increases, as there is more carbon to burn
It increases, so it is easier to set alight
It does not change for any hydrocarbon
It decreases, so it is harder to ignite

questions.explanation: Large molecules are hard to vaporise, and a fuel must vaporise before it will burn.

questions.stem: What colour change is seen when bromine water reacts with an alkene?

options.text: Colourless bromine water turns orange in colour
Orange bromine water is decolourised to colourless
Orange bromine water turns a cloudy white colour
Orange bromine water turns a blue-black colour

questions.explanation: Bromine water starts orange, and the alkene reacts with the bromine so the colour disappears.

questions.stem: Which equation shows the complete combustion of methane, CH₄?

options.text: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 4H₂O
2CH₄ + 4O₂ → CO₂ + 4H₂O
CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O

questions.explanation: Carbon: 1 and 1. Hydrogen: 4 and 4. Oxygen: 4 and 4. The equation is balanced.

questions.stem: Cracking one molecule of C₁₀H₂₂ produces one molecule of C₂H₄. What is the other product?

options.text: C₈H₁₆, treating the alkane as CₙH₂ₙ
C₁₀H₁₈, since only hydrogen is removed
C₁₂H₂₆, adding the two formulae up
C₈H₁₈, so that all the atoms balance

questions.stem: Liquefied petroleum gases are used in portable camping stoves. Which property makes them suitable?

options.text: They are highly flammable and ignite very easily
They have high boiling points and do not evaporate
They are very viscous and pour out slowly and safely
They contain the largest hydrocarbon molecules of all

questions.explanation: Small hydrocarbon molecules vaporise readily and are highly flammable, which is exactly what a small stove needs.

questions.stem: The products of cracking include alkanes. What is the other type of hydrocarbon produced?

options.text: Only more alkanes, but smaller in size
Alcohols, that contain oxygen as well
Alkenes, a more reactive hydrocarbon
Polymers, made of very long chains

questions.explanation: The specification states that the products of cracking include alkanes and another type of hydrocarbon called alkenes.
